subject: computer-science

items.q: Does a strong password alone keep you safe?
items.correct: No — security needs layers (updates, 2FA, caution with phishing).
items.misconception: Yes, a strong password guarantees safety.
items.why: No single measure is foolproof; defence in depth is needed.

items.q: Is every type of malware a virus?
items.correct: No — a virus is one type; others include worms, trojans and ransomware.
items.misconception: Yes, all malware is a virus.
items.random_wrong: Encryption is a type of malware.
items.why: 'Malware' is the umbrella term; viruses self-replicate by attaching to files.

items.correct: Scrambles data so only authorised users can read it.
items.why: Encryption protects confidentiality; the data is unreadable without the key.
